name: adcm-toolkits
description: Public ADCM toolkits: the Council multi-advisor deliberation framework (generic, bring-your-own-context), a code-project context generator that builds a lazy-loading, refreshable knowledge base of a codebase (architecture, API surface, data models, config, security, conventions), a business context generator that interviews the owner and researches the business website to produce an installable, lazy-loading business-context skill (identity, offering, market, brand voice, sales, operations, objectives, plus a confidential internal file), and an execution-prompt architect that turns goals + deep code analysis into a six-document execution plan (executive proposal, master plan, detailed plan, timeframe plan with critical path and week-by-week schedule, task tracker, execution protocol) with self-contained copy-paste prompts per wave (each embeds a SCOPE manifest: files to modify with why, impact census of shared-surface consumers, the reuse/extraction plan, freshness checks — clean sessions execute without re-analyzing the project), a comment policy that keeps decisions in the plan instead of the code, a code-simplifier pass over every wave's integrated diff before the final DoD run and an optional single-file HTML with a CSS Gantt timeline. The business context generator also mines EXISTING sources before interviewing — sales decks, database migrations and price catalogs, quoting tools, a sibling venture's execution docs, brand tokens and memory files — fanning out one sub-agent per source family under the same 20-agent tiered protocol, consolidating a fact sheet where every fact carries its source path, date, confidence and confidentiality class, and then interviewing only for the UNKNOWNs. The execution-prompt architect documents the two container homes (own ventures and client work), the three supported positions of ai-brain and the symlink the artifact-guard Stop hook requires, the bilingual document-name sets (Spanish default for Spanish-speaking ventures, task.md/execute.md never translated), and prompts.html as a second canonical artifact regenerated from execute.md §7 instead of hand-edited. The context generator also emits a usage-map (shared surfaces → consumer census) and supports delta refreshes (--update) at wave close. Use for structured multi-perspective decisions, to document a codebase or a business, or to plan and prompt large tasks and migrations, and an agentic-SEO reporter that audits a live site for how well search engines AND AI agents can find, read and use it — combining the free is-agentic.com agent-readiness score (reported unmodified, with its scan date) with local checks it does not perform (llms.txt, hreflang reciprocity and content parity, JSON-LD validity and retired types, schema coverage, sitemap health, AI-crawler posture in robots.txt, text visible without JavaScript), writing findings ranked by traffic impact where each one carries the command that reproduces it; it honors per-project confidentiality rules, so it never recommends publishing a price, cost or manufacturing detail the project marked internal, and it refuses to emit its own report if that report would leak one. Use for structured multi-perspective decisions, to document a codebase or a business, to plan and prompt large tasks and migrations, or to audit a site for search and AI-agent visibility. It also ships a design-direction architect that runs the research phase before any UI is built: it interviews the owner (auto-filling from an installed business or code-project context skill), mines four real sources — the Framer template marketplace including each template's live demo, Pinterest via a browser with its filter chips, 21st.dev components/themes/templates through the magic MCP, and Pexels photo and video assets filtered to the project palette — scores at least fifteen candidates on nine dimensions, and presents five finalists from two or more sources instead of settling for the first hit. When the business sells something it runs a second, separate search for the product/service section and the quote-or-checkout flow. The output is a reusable reference pack in .design/ (brief, scored references, tokens, commercial surface, asset manifest with real-photo markers, decision log and screenshots) that the building skills consume; it never builds the site itself. It also ships an artifact courier that moves the delivery close of a session off the expensive main model: one Sonnet sub-agent runs the plan-page generators (plans.html and prompts.html are produced by script, never hand-rendered) and republishes every stale claude.ai Artifact listed in the project's artifacts.json (in place after reading the live version, or re-issued as a new artifact above ~300 KB with the previous URL kept), stamps published_at, version and sha256 so the artifact-guard Stop hook trusts sub-agent publishes, sends the visual-check screenshots and returns the phone-tappable links block the main session pastes verbatim. Every skill now carries the pure-orchestrator hard rule: the main session briefs sub-agents with an explicit model, reads their returns and decides, and only does the work itself when the owner says so.
